question: A long strategy chat has drifted off track, and it keeps re-deriving background the team will still need next week. Which two actions are appropriate here? Select two.
options: A) Start a fresh chat that restates the current goal and carries only the material still needed.
B) Switch over to the lightest and fastest tier so that continuing this long conversation costs less.
C) Move the durable background into a Project, so later chats begin from it without redoing it.
D) Carry on in the same chat and restate the goal more forcefully every time answers drift off.
E) Delete earlier messages from the chat so that older material stops shaping the newer replies.
correct_answers: A) Start a fresh chat that restates the current goal and carries only the material still needed.
C) Move the durable background into a Project, so later chats begin from it without redoing it.
explanations: Correct. Restarting with a tight restatement clears accumulated drift and keeps only the context that is still relevant.
Incorrect. A cheaper tier does not fix drift, and it does not persist the background the team will need again.
Correct. Background needed again next week is durable context, and a Project is where durable context belongs.
Incorrect. Repeating the goal more forcefully in a drifting conversation rarely recovers it and adds to an already crowded context.
Incorrect. Pruning messages is not how a drifting chat is repaired, and it does not make the background durable for next week.
